text: Automatically reviews new pull requests once installed on a repo
quote: Once installed, cubic automatically reviews new pull requests.

text: Can trigger a review on a pre-existing PR via a PR comment command
quote: To review a PR that was opened _before_ you installed the app, comment: `@cubic-dev-ai review this PR`.

text: Offers an 'Ultrareview' deep-review mode using more capable models for risky/complex changes
quote: Ultrareview runs a longer review using cubic's most capable review models, which is useful for risky migrations, security-sensitive changes, or complex refactors.

text: Can generate a fix for a flagged issue and push it directly to the PR branch
quote: cubic generates the fix and pushes it to your PR branch.

text: Developers can reply to review comments to ask for clarification and get contextual answers
quote: Reply to a review comment to ask for clarification:

text: Supports auto-approval of PRs that meet a defined review policy
quote: Enable [auto-approval](/ai-review/auto-approval) to let cubic approve PRs that meet your review policy.

text: Provides an official CLI that reviews local diffs before push and generates a fix prompt for coding agents
quote: The **cubic CLI** reviews local changes before you push. It finds bugs and generates a prompt that your coding agent can use to fix them.

text: Ships an MCP server so coding agents can read findings, request reviews, and triage issues
quote: Connect cubic's MCP server to your coding agent to read review findings and codebase context, request PR reviews, and triage PR or codebase scan issues.

text: Supports custom agents encoding org-specific review rules enforced across PRs
quote: Custom agents are review rules that enforce your organization's specific best practices across pull requests.

text: Learns from developer replies and thumbs up/down reactions to calibrate future feedback
quote: cubic automatically learns when you: Reply to its comments... React to suggestions: Thumbs up/down help cubic calibrate what's useful vs noise

text: Uses a versioned cubic.yaml config file for review behavior, ignore patterns, and custom agents
quote: `cubic.yaml` lives in the root of your repository and becomes the source of truth for AI review behavior, ignore patterns, PR descriptions, and custom agents.

text: Runs codebase-wide scans deploying many AI agents to find bugs and vulnerabilities across the repo
quote: Codebase scans deploy thousands of AI agents to find bugs and vulnerabilities across your repository.

text: Generates an AI-indexed, searchable wiki of the codebase with architecture diagrams and source links
quote: cubic's AI wiki automatically indexes your codebase and produces searchable wikis, complete with links to source code, architecture diagrams, and more.

text: Can hide test files from the PR diff/file tree to focus review on implementation changes
quote: Focus on implementation changes by hiding test files from the PR diff and file tree.

text: Coding agents can manage subscription, seats, and roles through cubic's MCP integration
quote: You can now ask your coding agent to check your cubic subscription, manage team seats and roles, and purchase more seats without leaving your MCP client.

text: Exposes an Analytics API with PR-level data on flagged/fixed issues and AI-authored code volume
quote: The Analytics API gives you PR-level data on how many issues were flagged, how many were fixed, how much AI code was authored, etc.

text: Provides 'skills' giving coding agents instructions for reviewing code and using team codebase context
quote: cubic skills give your coding agent instructions for reviewing code, handling PR comments, and using your team's codebase context.
